items.title: AI Driven Personalized Learning and Learning Analytics in Higher Education: Effects on Student Engagement, Achievement and Research Integrity
items.abstract: The study aimed to examine the effect of personalized learning through artificial intelligence (AI) and learning analytics on student engagement and learning outcomes of higher education institutes in Pakistan with implications for Research Integrity at these institutes. Adopting a mixed methods approach, quantitative data gathered from 500 students from an undergraduate science program, with semi structured interviews with 30 students for the qualitative data. The descriptive statistics indicated that the mean engagement scores for those students who have access to AI based personalized learnings were significantly higher than the mean scores of students in traditional learning setting; it is from these that an increase in engagement by the students were observed. There was an improvement in Academic achievement as well, as indicated by higher grade point averages, and improved scores of the formative assessments. The regression analysis results showed that AI (personalized learning) and learning analytics (β = .41; p < .001) were among its most important models that were significant in predicting the variable of academic achievement; the analysis of correlation results showed that there was a good positive correlation between the variables of engagement and academic achievement (r = .63, p < .01). The qualitative results corroborated this as students felt there was a significant increase in motivation, personalized feedback, and adaptive learning pathways as being the most beneficial aspects of the AI integration. Issues were identified that could interfere in successful implementation: Data privacy concerns, uneven access to technology and insufficient faculty preparation. According to this study, personalized learning & learning analytics with AI have proved to be significant drivers of student engagement & academic performance, provided that the ethical issues and infrastructure are sorted out and this may influence the way research integrity and rigor will be upheld within Higher Education Institutions. The findings herein expand the conversation taking place around the role of AI in education and highlight the need to embed learning analytics in a learning design practice, to create inclusive and effective learning spaces.

items.title: AI Pedagogy in Higher Education: A Scoping Review of Competencies, Enactments, and Ethical Governance
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in higher education, yet the pedagogical field intended to organise its use remains conceptually underdeveloped. This scoping review mapped and synthesised peer-reviewed literature on AI pedagogy in higher education, using teacher education as the primary analytic lens. Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR reporting principles, searches were conducted across ten databases and publisher platforms for literature published between 2022 and March 2026. Of 956 records screened, 191 studies were included. Data charting and synthesis combined deductive coding, an a priori codebook, AI-assisted coding in Atlas. ti, and human inductive open coding. Six interrelated themes emerged: AI pedagogy is contextually produced rather than universally defined; conceptualised through pedagogical integration, competence, and borrowed theories rather than a settled standalone theory; enacted mainly through augmentation-oriented practices and generative AI tools; and associated with changing teacher professionalism, ethical mediation, governance, structural constraints, and a rapidly expanding but methodologically uneven evidence base. The review rejects purely technical, universal, or tool-centred models of innovation. Instead, it positions AI pedagogy as a context-specific, human-led, competence-rich, and governance-aware form of teaching in which AI supports planning, feedback, adaptation, and reflection without displacing human educational responsibility, especially within teacher education contexts and programmes.

items.title: AI-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality-Emotional Attachment-Loyalty Pathway in 2025-2026
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although the retailer-specific investment figures cited in an earlier draft have not been independently substantiated. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). We discuss a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents (β = 0.289, p = 0.001) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents (β = −0.023, p = 0.811). Age-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51.2% of the variance in loyalty (R2 = 0.512) and has positive predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.289). Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty.

items.title: AI-Based Waste Classification and Smart Waste Management Systems: Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Rapid urban growth and the corresponding rise in municipal solid waste have intensified the need for efficient and scalable waste management solutions. Conventional segregation practices, which largely rely on manual intervention, are often time-consuming, inconsistent, and unsuitable for handling large volumes of waste. In recent years, advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Deep Learning (DL) have facilitated the development of intelligent systems capable of automating waste classification and monitoring processes. This survey provides a detailed review of 13 research studies published between 2021 and 2025, with a focus on AI-driven approaches for waste management. It examines a range of techniques, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), object detection frameworks, and hybrid learning models, along with the datasets, evaluation metrics, and system designs employed in these works. A comparative assessment is carried out to analyze the performance, advantages, and limitations of the existing methodologies. The review further identifies critical research gaps, such as the absence of standardized benchmark datasets, limited real-time implementation, lack of multimodal sensor integration, and insufficient emphasis on model interpretability. Based on these findings, the paper outlines potential future directions, including the adoption of edge-based AI systems, integration with IoT-enabled smart infrastructure, and the use of advanced detection models to support scalable and efficient waste management in smart city environments.

items.title: AI-Mediated Translation and Interference in Arabic: Revisiting Toury’s Law in the Age of Digital Language
items.abstract: Thanks to artificial intelligence and machine translation technologies, the volume and speed of translation production have increased. However, these technologies also raise questions about the impact of dominant digital languages on less resourced ones. Many languages remain underrepresented in multilingual modelling due to the limited availability of digital language resources. This results in an uneven linguistic representation in natural language processing and AI models, which, in turn, leads to an asymmetry in linguistic influence, as evidenced by the literature. This study investigates linguistic interference in Arabic translation within digital environments, drawing on Toury’s (2012) Law of Interference. It addresses a critical gap by examining, from a qualitative perspective, how uneven language representation in automated translation environments may shape the quality of Arabic translations. It argues that the unequal distribution of digital language resources may contribute to the transfer of source-language features into Arabic translations. Methodologically, the study adopts an exploratory qualitative approach, analysing a small corpus of 100 Arabic translations from English and French, including human and machine-generated translations, focusing on three dimensions of interference: lexical, syntactic and discursive. The findings show repeating patterns of source-oriented elements, including the incorrect use of cataphoric construction and the coordinator واو, the excessive use of periphrastic constructions and the reduction of stylistic adaptation. Similar patterns were observed in machine translation outputs and online Arabic content, suggesting that AI systems reproduce linguistic tendencies already present in digitally circulating texts. The study highlights the need for greater attention to online high-quality Arabic resources.

items.title: Al-Qur’an dan Keseimbangan Antara Artificial Intelligence dan Spiritual Intelligence: Rekonstruksi Tekno-Spiritualitas dalam Perspektif Quranic Worldview
items.abstract: Ekskalasi teknologi kecerdasan buatan (Artificial Intelligence/AI) pada era modernitas akhir telah membawa transformasi multidimensional yang tidak hanya menyentuh aspek teknis-utilitarian, melainkan merambah ranah eksistensial, antropologis, dan epistemologis manusia. Kecenderungan peradaban modern yang didominasi oleh cara berpikir belahan otak kiri yang bercorak mekanistis, kalkulatif, dan reduksionis berisiko mengikis kesadaran transendental serta memicu krisis kehampaan spiritualitas (spiritual emptiness). Artikel jurnal tingkat doktoral ini bertujuan merekonstruksi secara komprehensif paradigma keseimbangan antara Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan Spiritual Intelligence (SI) melalui kacamata pandangan hidup Al-Qur'an (Quranic Worldview). Menggunakan metode tafsir tematik konseptual (maudhu’i) yang diintegrasikan dengan hermeneutika filosofis dan pendekatan maqāṣid al-syarī‘ah, penelitian ini membedah status ontologis, batas epistemologis, dan orientasi aksiologis AI dan SI. Eksplorasi teks suci difokuskan pada dialog arketipikal kekhalifahan Nabi Adam as. dan kritik teknofetisisme patung anak sapi emas Samiri, yang diperkuat dengan analisis eksegetis terhadap beberapa ayat ayng lain. Penelitian ini juga merumuskan pilar-pilar kecerdasan spiritual Qur'ani: kesadaran diri, transendensi, makna hidup, nilai etis, dan kesadaran holistik. Hasil kajian menyimpulkan bahwa AI secara ontologis berstatus instrumen profan aksidental (khādim) yang terikat pada hukum komputasi simbolik dan probabilistik, sehingga klaim transhumanisme mengenai kesadaran mesin (ensoulment) ditolak secara mutlak karena ketiadaan hembusan rūḥ ilahiah dan fakultas qalb. Keseimbangan peradaban tercapai manakala lompatan AI ditundukkan di bawah kepemimpinan aksiologis SI yang berakar pada tauhid, keadilan (‘adl), kemaslahatan (maṣlaḥah), dan kesadaran human-in-the-loop, guna mengarahkan sains menuju terwujudnya martabat manusia seutuhnya (al-insān al-kāmil).

items.title: An Assessment of Green Management and Artificial Intelligence in Sustainable Business Management
items.abstract: The aim of this study is to examine academic publications on green management published in 2024, identifying key research themes, findings, and relationships with sustainability, environmental performance, and green human resource management. A qualitative research design based on document analysis was adopted for the investigation. Data were gathered from 23 academic publications retrieved via Google Scholar using the keyword “green management”. Selected publications underwent rigorous content analysis, and findings were synthesized thematically alongside geographical and sectoral distributions. China represented the largest share, accounting for 39.1% of all reviewed publications. Research predominantly focused on the corporate sector, followed by higher education, manufacturing, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Notably, none of the examined studies directly addressed green artificial intelligence. The findings indicate that green management is strongly associated with green innovation, environmental performance, resource efficiency, employee environmentally responsible behaviors, and overall organizational sustainability. Green technology adoption, organizational culture, and environmental regulations also emerged as critical drivers. Ultimately, the results underscore the necessity of integrating environmental objectives into core organizational strategies. Future research should explore green management across diverse national and sectoral contexts.

items.abstract: This conceptual working paper examines whether the New Human Rights (Neue Menschenrechte, NMR) approach developed by Jean-Pol Martin displays the characteristics of an emerging school of thought.It proposes five analytical criteria: a shared theoretical core, an interconnected vocabulary, a recognizable mode of inquiry, sustained collective activity, and autonomous contributions beyond the founder. Drawing on selected primary texts, publisher descriptions and public practitioner accounts, the paper identifies indications of these features in publications, training activities and distinct applications of the framework.The conceptual architecture connects an organism-based understanding of human beings, six basic need domains, a universal normative commitment to enabling their satisfaction, and a process model linking exploration, information processing, conceptualization and agency. Learning by Teaching (LdL) and human–AI cooperation are situated within this architecture.The article’s specific contribution is to shift attention from an individual theoretical project to the development of a shared intellectual and practical tradition. Within the ongoing sequence of papers on LdL, NMR and human–AI cooperation, it connects the reconstruction of Martin’s work with a prospective collective research programme.The paper distinguishes autonomous development within the project from independent reception outside its originating network. It concludes that “an emerging NMR school of thought” is a defensible interpretation of the documented activities and identifies questions for further conceptual and empirical investigation.Prepared by Jean-Pol Martin in collaboration with ChatGPT. items.title: Anatomical Review: Optimizing and Harnessing Workflows — A Section-by-Section Reading of Noguer i Alonso (2026), Task-Specific Combinations of Humans, Software, and AI Agents
items.abstract: This anatomical review systematically dissects Noguer i Alonso's (2026) framework for hybrid workflows integrating human decision makers (H), specified computational procedures (D), and adaptive artificial delegates (A). The paper advances a principled account of agentification, deagentification, automation, and harnessing, grounded in a partial order on delegation profiles rather than scalar autonomy scores, and supported by formal results on permission restriction, invariant preservation, retry exposure, advisory isolation, and the proceduralization gap. While the contribution offers valuable conceptual clarity for task-specific authority allocation in agentic systems, the review identifies limitations in empirical scope (synthetic examples only), the open problem of semantic promotion, and the transferability of formal guarantees to production environments. Implications for AI governance, hybrid intelligence, and institutional design in Global South contexts are discussed.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Supply Chain Management: Applications, Evidence, Implementation Constraints, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly investigated as decision-support technologies for supply chain management (SCM), yet their value depends on the nature of the decision, data availability, organisational capability and the methods used to evaluate outcomes. This critical narrative review examines applications across demand forecasting, inventory planning, sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, risk management and sustainability. It brings together relevant peer-reviewed reviews, conceptual contributions and empirical studies, and distinguishes evidence from operational deployments from results reported in literature syntheses or simulations. The literature supports the practical relevance of data-driven prediction, pattern detection and decision augmentation, but it does not establish uniform improvements in cost, forecast accuracy, resilience or environmental performance across settings. Reviewed research also identifies integration costs, fragmented data, process misalignment, model drift, limited transparency and governance concerns as barriers to realising benefits. Recent work on generative AI broadens possible applications to document-intensive processes, synthetic scenarios and interactive decision support, while indicating that field-based validation remains limited. A process-oriented framework is proposed in which analytics inform planning, procurement, manufacturing, distribution and inventory decisions under continuous human oversight. The review argues that useful evaluations should compare AI-supported decisions against relevant operational baselines, account for service levels and cost trade-offs, and document transferability across sectors and resource settings. Future research should prioritise longitudinal field studies, cross-organisational coordination, responsible deployment and context-sensitive applications in emerging economies.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Capabilities and Organizational Sustainability of Retail Outlets in Port Harcourt: A Drive for Renewable Hope in Smart Economies
items.abstract: The study examined artificial intelligence capabilities and organizational sustainability of retail outlets in Port Harcourt. The objectives of the study were to examine the relationship between dimensions of artificial intelligence capabilities such as CCTV analytics, chatbots and automated processing; and measures of organizational sustainability in terms of Environmental sustainability and Economic sustainability of retail outlets in Port Harcourt. Thus, the study was anchored on Diffusion of Innovation theoretical foundation. The study adopted the cross-sectional survey research design. The accessible population of the study was Sixteen (16) retail outlets currently operating in Port Harcourt. The entire population was used as the study sample. Thus, the study was census research which involves using the entire population rather than drawing a sample from it. Structured questionnaire served as the instrument for data collection. A total of sixty-four (64) copies of the validated questionnaire were distributed to the targeted audience. The researcher was able to retrieve fifty-six (56) copies of the entire validated questionnaire distributed. Arithmetic mean and standard deviation were used for the research question analyses, while the test of hypotheses was done using Spearman rank order correlation with the aid of SPSS Version 24.0. It was found that there is a significant positive relationship between artificial intelligence capabilities and organizational sustainability of retail outlets in Port Harcourt. It was concluded that leveraging artificial intelligence powered tools such as CCTV analytics, chatbots and automated processing, retailers can enhance operational efficiency, improve customer experiences and gain valuable insights into market trends. Consequently, it was recommended that operators of retail outlets should utilize automated system to track inventory level, reduce waste and optimize stock replenishment.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Eurasian Higher Education: An Empirical Study of Student Practices
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has penetrated higher education not through official strategies but via students’ and faculty members’ personal devices, catching most universities off guard. This article presents empirical data from a large-scale survey conducted between March and April 2026 across six post-Soviet countries (Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Armenia, Tajikistan). The study provides a systematic cross-national analysis of student AI use patterns in the Eurasian higher education space, complementing recent single-country studies in the region. The sample included 478 students. The study measured frequency of AI use, perceived risks, compatibility with educational values, and the presence of institutional regulatory mechanisms. The results show that 78 % of students regularly use generative AI, yet only 32 % of universities have an official policy in this area. A deep disciplinary divide emerges: students fall into two roughly equal profiles – “pragmatic techs” (daily users with low ethical anxiety) and “reflective humanists” (cautious users with a strong demand for ethical frameworks). The main barrier to AI adoption is not technological infrastructure but the absence of regulatory and social technologies. The article offers discipline-differentiated recommendations for universities in non-Western contexts.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence to Support Academic Writing: A Systematic Literature Review of English Second Language Students in Higher Education
items.abstract: Sophisticated AI applications like ChatGPT and Grammarly offer distinct advantages for enhancing writing proficiency. They assist users in conceptualising ideas, organising material, and refining writing style, whereas Grammarly focuses on improving grammar, punctuation, and clarity with context-aware recommendations. This is particularly relevant for students who are non-native English speakers, as it supports them and helps bridge educational disparities. While these instruments markedly enhance scholarly writing abilities, their efficacy in tertiary education remains a subject of debate. Recent occurrences of academic dishonesty associated with the improper use of generative AI technologies have negatively impacted higher education. This study assesses the impact of artificial intelligence on enhancing academic writing abilities in students who are not native English speakers. In accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) criteria, this study consolidates evidence from scholarly literature, policy reports, and institutional case analyses. Keywords, synonyms, and subject headings were employed to query three electronic databases from 2021 to 2025. The electronic repositories included Scopus, Emerald Insight, Google Scholar, and ProQuest. The evaluation of the publications was conducted through titles and abstracts, followed by an assessment of the full-text papers against the qualifying criteria. The results were derived and amalgamated into a narrative synthesis from selected publications. The results underscored AI's ability to customise and improve the educational experience for learners.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Use in Honours Research: Implications for Supervision Relationships, Knowledge Development, and Research Quality
items.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in higher education has reshaped how students engage with academic research, particularly at Honours level, where students transition from structured undergraduate learning to independent postgraduate research. Guided by Self‑Regulated Learning (SRL) theory, this study examines how reliance on AI by Honours research students influences the supervisor-supervisee relationship, the quality of research produced, and the extent of knowledge gained through the research process. SRL theory emphasises learners’ ability to plan, monitor, and reflect on their own learning, which is central to successful postgraduate research development. This study adopts a conceptual and literature‑based review methodology, drawing on peer‑reviewed studies on AI use in higher education, literature on postgraduate supervision, and academic integrity and research skills development frameworks, with specific attention to Honours‑level contexts. The documents were analysed using thematic content analysis, focusing on self‑regulatory behaviours, supervisory interaction, research skill development, and learning depth. The findings suggest that limited and transparent use of AI can support honours students by reducing surface‑level cognitive load and assisting with language clarity. However, excessive reliance on AI may undermine key self‑regulation processes, weaken critical thinking, and reduce meaningful engagement with supervisors. Supervisors may struggle to accurately assess students’ understanding, potentially straining trust and feedback processes. The review further indicates that over‑reliance on AI risks producing research that is technically adequate but conceptually shallow, with reduced long‑term knowledge acquisition. The study concludes that clear supervision practices and explicit guidance on responsible AI use are necessary to ensure that AI supports, rather than replaces, the self‑regulated learning essential for high‑quality Honours‑level research.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of postoperative voiding dysfunction following midurethral sling
items.abstract: Purpose of review Midurethral sling (MUS) surgery is the standard procedure for stress urinary incontinence, offering favorable long-term outcomes. Despite its success, postoperative voiding dysfunction – manifesting as urinary retention, elevated post-void residuals (PVRs), slow or weak stream, hesitancy, or the need for prolonged catheterization – remains a clinically significant complication that is difficult to predict using traditional risk stratification. Conventional methods, including history, physical examination, PVR measurement, and selective urodynamics, provide limited individualized predictive power and fail to integrate the complex interplay of patient, anatomical, and surgical factors. Recent findings Artificial intelligence and machine learning offer a promising approach to addressing this gap by analyzing multidimensional datasets to forecast individualized risk and guide perioperative management. While artificial intelligence applications in pelvic floor surgery have demonstrated utility in predicting general surgical outcomes, validated models specifically targeting post-MUS voiding dysfunction are lacking. Development of such predictive tools will require high-quality multicenter datasets, careful algorithm selection, and validation. Summary Integrating artificial intelligence into clinical practice has the potential to enhance preoperative counseling, support shared decision-making, optimize surgical planning, and ultimately improve patient outcomes. This perspective highlights the unmet need for predictive modeling of voiding dysfunction after MUS, outlines the promise of artificial intelligence, and emphasizes the importance of responsible implementation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence‐Assisted Ultrasound for Sarcopenia Assessment: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Muscle ultrasound offers a portable, non‐invasive, and cost‐effective option for sarcopenia assessment, but operator dependency limits its standardization. Artificial intelligence (AI) may help automate and improve ultrasound‐based muscle evaluation. This scoping review aims to map the current landscape of AI‐assisted ultrasound for sarcopenia assessment, including research trends, methods, clinical uses and performance, and to suggest future work. Methods Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines and the PRISMA‐ScR checklist, we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, ProQuest, CNKI, WanFang Data, Yiigle, VIP, and Sinomed up to July 25, 2026. Two researchers independently selected studies and extracted data. Results Thirty studies were included. This field is developing rapidly, with 76.7% of studies published in the last 3 years, primarily from Spain and China. Model development and validation studies (43.3%) were most common. U‐Net and its variants were the predominant AI architectures, mainly for image segmentation. B‐mode ultrasound with high‐frequency linear probes was frequently used. The rectus femoris was the most assessed muscle for sarcopenia (73.3%). AI‐integrated models for sarcopenia diagnosis achieved AUCs of 0.640–0.950. Reported Dice coefficients for muscle segmentation ranged from 0.73 to 0.99. In‐house datasets were used in 66.7% of the studies, and global classification labels were the most frequent annotation strategy (46.7%). Conclusions AI‐assisted ultrasound shows potential for objective and scalable sarcopenia assessment but remains early‐stage. Operator dependency in image acquisition has not been fully resolved. Further investigation should determine the added value of integrating multimodal imaging, combining diverse AI techniques, and evaluating multiple muscle groups. Future efforts should deepen image‐processing strategies to extract clinically relevant features and facilitate standardized, scalable implementation in clinical practice.

items.title: Assessing the Empirical Evidence for Loss of Control from Agentic General-Purpose AI
items.abstract: Theoretical literature warns that advanced generalist agentic systems might pursue instrumental goals that are misaligned with human preferences, thus posing risks of irreversible loss of human control. The EU's Code of Practice for General-Purpose AI lists loss of control as a systemic risk that must be assessed, yet no structured assessment of the quality of the empirical evidence for this risk exists. This study fills that gap. We evaluate 19 recent empirical studies across eight properties identified from threat models (such as strategic deception, situational awareness, and autonomous replication), assessing the quality of evidence across three dimensions: construct validity, content validity, and external validity. Our central finding is that the current body of evidence supports a judgment of loss of control as "weakly plausible." In our framework, 'plausibility' denotes the strength and direction of available evidence, not a probability estimate. Emerging evidence exists across multiple properties. No study clears the validity thresholds for a stronger judgment that a property is present; a single study clears them only for a negative-direction judgment (against situational awareness). Validity gaps, particularly in external validity, are widespread. Therefore, our findings highlight the need for more rigorous evaluations of agentic general-purpose AI systems. However, for the most dangerous properties, high external validity may be structurally unachievable under responsible research practices, reflecting a ceiling on feasible evidence rather than absence of the capability. Furthermore, as AI capabilities advance rapidly, empirical assessments may systematically lag behind the capability frontier. Our framework provides a structured baseline for ongoing monitoring as capabilities advance.

items.title: Beyond Automation: Human–Technology Synergy and the Future of Work
items.abstract: Rapid technological advancement is transforming contemporary organizations and reshaping the future of work. Artificial intelligence (AI), automation, digital communication technologies, and data-driven systems increasingly influence organizational structures, managerial practices, employee experiences, and workplace interactions. While these developments offer important opportunities to improve efficiency, flexibility, and innovation, they also raise significant concerns about employee well-being, ethical responsibility, privacy, surveillance, and workforce adaptation. This chapter examines the evolving relationship between humans and technology from a human-centered perspective. First, it briefly discusses the historical evolution of workplace technologies, from the Industrial Revolution to the current era of AI-driven digital transformation. Second, the chapter explores human–technology synergy and emphasizes the importance of collaboration and complementarity between human and technological capabilities in organizational settings. Third, it examines the growing role of human-centered technology in supporting employee well-being, inclusivity, participation, and ethical organizational practices. The chapter also discusses the organizational implications of AI integration, including changes in job roles, decision-making processes, workplace flexibility, and employee adaptation. Finally, key challenges associated with technology integration, such as algorithmic bias, workplace surveillance, digital fatigue, and technological dependency, are addressed alongside potential future directions of human–technology collaboration. Overall, the chapter argues that successful digital transformation requires organizations to balance technological advancement with human values, needs, and capabilities. The long-term sustainability of workplace technologies depends not only on operational efficiency but also on organizations’ ability to foster ethical, adaptive, and mutually beneficial relationships between humans and technology.

items.title: BEYOND CRIMINALISATION: DIGITAL VICTIMISATION AND VICTIM PROTECTION AGAINST AI DEEPFAKES IN INDONESIA
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) deepfakes enable the convincing imitation of an individual’s image or voice, creating risks that extend beyond the identification and punishment of offenders. This article examines how Indonesian law responds to digital victimisation and whether its remedies address reputational, psychological and social harm. Using normative legal research and a focused interdisciplinary literature review, it analyses the Electronic Information and Transactions Law, Personal Data Protection Law, Sexual Violence Crimes Law, the Criminal Code and criminal procedure reforms, including the 2026 Witness and Victim Protection Law. The analysis identifies three interconnected problems: harm may arise before distribution; protection depends on fitting conduct within fragmented offences; and criminal proceedings alone do not ensure rapid content containment or sustained recovery. It proposes a victim-centred response linking accessible reporting, lawful evidence preservation, timely platform action, risk-sensitive support and restitution where legal conditions are met. Rather than claiming an absence of relevant laws, the article argues that coordination and remedies should reflect the continuous nature of technology-facilitated harm. This framework offers a policy-oriented contribution to debates on digital victimology and access to justice in Indonesia.

items.title: Boosting Vocabulary Mastery: ChatGPT’s Role in Advancing EFL Learners’ Language Skills
items.abstract: This study attempted to implement artificial intelligence in language learning using the well-known ChatGPT. This study focused on measuring the effects of ChatGPT on vocabulary size and depth of knowledge. To collect the required data, 60 Omani intermediate EFL learners were divided equally into control and experimental groups. An updated vocabulary level test (UVLT), developed by Webb et al. (2017), and a Word Associate Test (WAT) developed by Read (1998) were used as the pretests to ensure the homogeneity of students’ vocabulary knowledge. Although both groups continued the traditional face-to-face training, the experimental group had the opportunity to use ChatGPT as a facilitator of vocabulary learning with the chance of tailored and personalized activities. The UVLT and WAT were administered again as posttests to compare learners’ performance after the treatment. The findings revealed that both groups showed increases in the posttest regarding vocabulary size, but the experimental group outperformed the control group remarkably. Although no progress was made in the depth of vocabulary by the control group, the experimental group performed significantly better. The findings are insightful for teachers, curriculum designers, students, researchers, institutions, and policymakers.

items.title: Bridging Skills Gaps in South African Manufacturing: Curriculum Relevance, Mentorship, and Workplace Learning in Apprenticeship Programs
items.abstract: This study examines how curriculum relevance and workplace-based mentorship influence apprenticeship outcomes in South Africa’s manufacturing industry, with a focus on persistent skills gaps between training provision and industry requirements. Guided by Objective 1, which seeks to examine the relevance and alignment of apprenticeship curricula with the skills, technologies, and competency demands of the manufacturing sector, and Objective 3, which explores the role of mentorship and workplace-based learning in supporting skills development, employability, and workplace readiness, the study investigates the extent to which current apprenticeship programs reflect contemporary manufacturing practices. A qualitative, multi-case research design was employed, drawing on in-depth interviews with stakeholders from public colleges, private training centres, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The findings reveal a sustained misalignment between formal apprenticeship curricula and modern manufacturing technologies, including automation, robotics, and advanced production systems, largely resulting from centralised curriculum control and limited institutional autonomy. In contrast, mentorship and workplace learning emerged as critical mechanisms for translating theoretical knowledge into practical competence, strengthening professional identity, and developing both technical and soft skills. However, the effectiveness of mentorship practices varies across institutional contexts, with colleges facing greater structural and policy constraints than SMEs and training centres. The study concludes that bridging skills gaps in South Africa’s manufacturing sector requires an integrated approach that combines responsive curriculum reform with structured, industry-embedded mentorship and authentic workplace learning opportunities, offering practical and theoretical contributions to vocational education and training scholarship.

items.title: Buyer programmes for company data: eligibility, prices and payment terms of 37 organisations, October 2026
items.abstract: Since 2026 AI data vendors, marketplaces and intermediaries have published programmes through which an ordinary company can sell or license its internal records for training AI models. This paper compares the published terms of 37 organisations with a public way in, as compiled in an open dataset reviewed on 16 October 2026, together with a register of the contract clauses 16 of them publish and a dated log of 110 market events. Twenty-four take company records, 17 of them buying for their own account. Of those 24, 14 publish a floor (median $100,000) and 9 a ceiling (median $1 million; highest $5 million). Eligibility rules are sparse: six publish a headcount minimum (mostly 20 to 40 employees), two a minimum of three years, three a rule about country or language, and eight say they take companies that are closing or closed. Where a time to payment is stated it runs from 7 days after the data passes review to about 60 days, and several programmes pay only on the buyer's acceptance. Exclusivity is stated by few and deletion terms by six; one programme's terms say deletion does not require deleting trained models. Ten publish structured introduction fees, up to $100,000 per deal. No published ceiling is backed by an independently reported payment of that size: one programme has payments confirmed by sellers, at tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars, and seven report their own. We describe the data, the classification and the limits of comparing posted terms. items.title: CAN ARTIFICIAL INFLUENCERS BE AUTHENTIC? THE ROLE OF AI DISCLOSURE IN THE AUTHENTICITY–TRUST–PURCHASE INTENTION PARADOX IN SOCIAL COMMERCE
items.abstract: The rapid emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in social media has introduced Artificial Influencers as a new form of digitally constructed endorser, challenging conventional assumptions about authenticity, trust, and consumer behaviour. Unlike human influencers, Artificial Influencers are technologically created personas whose appearance, personality, communication, and interactions can be deliberately designed and controlled. This raises an important question: Can consumers perceive an Artificial Influencer as authentic when they are aware of its artificial nature? The present study examines the role of AI disclosure in shaping perceived authenticity and explores how authenticity relates to consumer trust and purchase intention in the context of social commerce. The study specifically addresses an emerging authenticity–trust–purchase intention paradox, whereby consumers may recognise an influencer as artificial, perceive limitations in its authenticity, and nevertheless remain willing to trust its recommendations or consider purchasing promoted products. A quantitative, exploratory, and cross-sectional research design was adopted. Primary data were collected through a structured online questionnaire from 30 social-media users using non-probability convenience sampling. The questionnaire examined respondents’ social-media exposure, awareness of Artificial Influencers, perceptions of AI disclosure, perceived authenticity, consumer trust, and purchase intention. Frequency and percentage analysis were used to describe response patterns, while Spearman’s rank-order correlation was employed to examine associations among the principal constructs. Given the small sample size, the study is positioned as an exploratory investigation and does not seek to establish population-level generalisation or definitive causal relationships. The findings indicate that AI disclosure has a dual significance in consumer evaluation. While 73.3% of respondents supported AI disclosure always or in most cases, disclosure was also associated with increased scrutiny of recommendations and greater concerns regarding genuineness. At the same time, 73.3% of respondents indicated that an Artificial Influencer could be perceived as authentic under certain circumstances, particularly when communication was relatable and consistent. However, 70.0% reported that awareness of AI generation reduced their perception of authenticity to some degree. Consumer trust appeared to be conditional rather than automatic, with respondents emphasising transparency, credibility, consistency, product relevance, and information verification. Purchase intention was similarly cautious, with respondents indicating that willingness to purchase depended on the product and the credibility of the recommendation. The study concludes that artificiality and authenticity should not be treated as mutually exclusive concepts. Consumers may simultaneously recognise the technological construction of an Artificial Influencer, experience reduced perceptions of genuineness, and still regard the influencer as sufficiently credible to support trust and purchase consideration. The findings therefore provide preliminary support for the authenticity–trust–purchase intention paradox and suggest that AI disclosure functions not simply as a mechanism that reduces authenticity, but as a transparency cue that can coexist with scepticism. The study contributes to the emerging literature on AI-mediated influencer marketing by integrating AI disclosure, perceived authenticity, consumer trust, and purchase intention within a single exploratory framework. For marketers, the findings highlight the importance of transparent disclosure, credible and verifiable product information, consistent communication, and responsible consumer engagement when deploying Artificial Influencers in social commerce.

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT and DeepSeek in Oral Pathology Education and Evidence-Based Diagnostic Decision Support: A Pilot Study
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into healthcare education and clinical decision-support systems. While ChatGPT has demonstrated promising performance in medical and dental domains, comparative evidence regarding newer models such as DeepSeek remains limited, particularly in oral pathology. This pilot study aimed to compare the performance of ChatGPT and DeepSeek in oral pathology education and evidence-based diagnostic decision support. We conducted a cross-sectional comparative study from January to December 2025. We developed ten oral pathology educational questions and five standardised clinical case scenarios based on established dental curricula and authoritative oral pathology references. Identical prompts were submitted independently to ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Responses were anonymised and evaluated by three board-certified oral pathologists using a structured rubric assessing accuracy, completeness, clinical relevance, diagnostic reasoning, and evidence-based consistency. Each domain was scored on a 5-point Likert scale, with a maximum total score of 25. Statistical analyses included independent-samples t-tests, Cohen’s d effect sizes, and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) assessment. ChatGPT achieved a significantly higher mean total composite score than DeepSeek (23.2 ± 1.8 vs. 20.6 ± 2.4; p = 0.006; Cohen’s d = 1.15). ChatGPT also outperformed DeepSeek across all evaluation domains, including accuracy (4.72 ± 0.31 vs. 4.18 ± 0.52; p = 0.003), completeness (4.68 ± 0.37 vs. 4.10 ± 0.55; p = 0.005), clinical relevance (4.61 ± 0.42 vs. 4.09 ± 0.58; p = 0.011), diagnostic reasoning (4.58 ± 0.46 vs. 3.98 ± 0.63; p = 0.008), and evidence-based consistency (4.75 ± 0.29 vs. 4.16 ± 0.49; p = 0.002). Large effect sizes were observed across all domains. Inter-rater reliability demonstrated excellent agreement among evaluators (ICC = 0.87; 95% CI: 0.81–0.92). ChatGPT demonstrated superior performance compared with DeepSeek in oral pathology education and evidence-based diagnostic decision support. Its higher accuracy, completeness, clinical relevance, and consistency with established evidence suggest considerable potential as an adjunctive educational and clinical support tool. Nevertheless, human oversight remains essential to ensure accuracy and mitigate the risks associated with AI-generated outputs. Further large-scale studies incorporating real clinical cases and multimodal diagnostic data are warranted.

items.title: Comprehensive Strategies for Hospital Infection Control: A Systematic Review of Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens, Surveillance Systems, and Antimicrobial Stewardship Interventions
items.abstract: Despite the significant contribution of HAIs to increased morbidity, mortality, length of hospital stay, and escalating health care costs, they continue to be a major public health problem globally.New and fast spreading "MDROs" (Multidrug Resistant Pathogens) including MRSA (Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus), VRE (Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci), ESBL (Extended-spectrum β-lactamase) producing Enterobacteriaceae, CRE (carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae), Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa have further contributed to the complexity of infection management in hospital settings.Due to the various resistance mechanisms such as enzymatic degradation, induction of efflux pumps, alteration of permeability and biofilm formation, there are limited therapeutic options and poor clinical outcomes available for these pathogens.This systematic review will assess the effectiveness of complete hospital infection control with an emphasis on infection prevention and control (IPC) interventions, surveillance tools and antimicrobial stewardship programs (ASPs).The standard and transmission based precautions, environmental hygiene and device associated IPC bundles (CLABSI, CAUTI, VAP) are critical reviewed as basic IPC approaches.The use of advanced surveillance tools, such as Electronic Health Records (EHR) surveillance, Microbiological antibiogram development, and AIdriven predictive analytics for early detection and outbreak management are also discussed.In addition, the effect of antimicrobial stewardship interventions (formulary restriction, de-escalation, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) optimization, and WHO AWaRe classification integration) on trends in antimicrobial resistance and hospital outcomes are evaluated.Future tools for infection control that are emerging as a result of research are noted as being artificial intelligence, quick molecular diagnostics, and nanotechnology antimicrobial surfaces.However, there are still challenges to be addressed, such as the improper use of antibiotics, limited resources, and non-compliance with treatment by health personnel.It exposes the need for multi-disciplinary, integrated approaches that include IPC, surveillance, and stewardship to effectively support the fight against MDR pathogens and patient safety in health care systems worldwide.

items.title: Corporate Governance Practices in Ai-Powered Technologies: A Perspective of Engineering Students
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become increasingly integrated into educational, professional, and technological environments, creating opportunities for innovation while raising concerns regarding transparency, accountability, ethical responsibility, privacy, and governance. Despite the growing use of AI-powered technologies among university students, limited research has examined how engineering students perceive corporate governance practices associated with these technologies. This study explored the perceptions of undergraduate engineering students regarding corporate governance in AI-powered technologies. A descriptive quantitative research design employing a cross-sectional survey approach was utilized. Data were collected from ninety-two (92) undergraduate engineering students at Cebu Institute of Technology–University (CIT-University) using a structured questionnaire. Frequency counts, percentages, weighted means, and ranking procedures were used to analyze the data. The findings revealed that respondents demonstrated positive awareness of corporate governance principles in AI systems, particularly regarding ethical responsibility, accountability, transparency, and data governance. The respondents also expressed a generally favorable level of trust in organizations utilizing AI-powered technologies, although concerns regarding privacy protection, data security, and responsible AI implementation remained evident. Among the governance dimensions examined, accountability received the highest rating, followed by ethical governance and transparency. Furthermore, the results showed that engineering students generally practiced responsible AI use, particularly in avoiding technologies that violate ethical and privacy standards. Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude, were identified as the most commonly used AI-powered technologies among the respondents. The study concludes that engineering students recognize the importance of responsible AI governance and view accountability, ethical responsibility, and transparency as essential components of trustworthy AI systems. These findings may contribute to the development of governance policies, educational initiatives, and responsible AI practices within academic and technological environments.

items.title: Cross-media affective differences in online reviews: aspect-level evidence and a dual-pathway mechanism
items.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the micro-level structural differences in online review affect between social media and e-commerce platforms, exploring the underlying psychological mechanisms that drive consumers to selectively express polarised reviews across these media. Design/methodology/approach Utilising large language model-driven aspect-based sentiment analysis, this study quantifies an initial dataset of 65,493 smartphone online reviews from TikTok, Bilibili, Jingdong and Suning to identify aspect-level affective differences. To explain the observed differences, Study 2 draws on uses and gratifications theory and conducts a 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment, using wireless headphones as the focal product and TikTok and Taobao as the platforms, to examine how media environments moderate the translation of consumption experiences into review intentions. Findings Affective differences extend to specific cognitive attributes, with social media platforms exhibiting a significantly more negative and heterogeneous affective landscape, whereas e-commerce platforms demonstrate overwhelming positivity. These differences are driven by a dual-pathway mechanism. Social media platforms primarily activate self-enhancement motivation, which facilitates the translation of negative experiences into negative reviews while weakening the translation of positive experiences into positive reviews. Conversely, e-commerce platforms primarily activate economic motivation, which facilitates the translation of positive experiences into positive reviews while reducing the likelihood of negative experiences translating into negative reviews. Originality/value This study extends the investigation of review affect from within-medium comparisons to cross-media analysis. By shifting from macro-level indicators to micro-level attribute evidence, this study reveals a more comprehensive picture of cross-media affective bias. By extending the application of uses and gratifications theory from content consumption to content production, it offers a novel mechanistic explanation for this phenomenon.

items.abstract: Abstract: The availability of customer data, the advance of artificial intelligence (AI) and the growing importance of digital content and influencers have changed the tools that firms can use to increase sales. This narrative review examines how these three levers—data and analytics, AI-enabled personalization, and content and influencer marketing—contribute to sales growth, and under which conditions they generate results. Peer-reviewed studies and reference works published up to 2023 were analyzed qualitatively. The literature indicates that marketing analytics improves decisions on targeting, pricing and resource allocation; that AI supports personalization at scale, from mechanical automation to analytical and feeling-oriented applications; and that content and influencer marketing build engagement, trust and purchase intention when they are relevant and credible. Generative AI, which gained prominence in 2023, expands content production and customer interaction capabilities but also raises concerns regarding accuracy, transparency and ethics. The review concludes that these levers produce the greatest effect when combined in an integrated system in which data informs content and personalization, and results are measured and fed back into decisions. It also emphasizes that privacy, trust and human judgment remain essential conditions for sustainable sales growth.

items.title: De-identifying company workspace exports in the data holder's browser: design and benchmark results
items.abstract: Company records such as chat workspaces, mailboxes, documents and tables are proposed as training data for language models, and they carry identifiers of employees, customers and other organisations. This report describes a rule-based de-identification engine that runs entirely in the data holder's browser, so that raw records, the people learned from them and the key behind every pseudonym stay on the holder's computer. It combines the people an export names in its own structure, pattern detectors validated by check digits, cues and a public-domain name lexicon, and the holder's own lists. It writes stand-ins from a keyed HMAC-SHA-256, scoped to each file by default, holds every table row to a group of at least 11, screens content for special categories, and rereads its output with a second check that has no memory of the first pass. On the held-out split of the Text Anonymization Benchmark (127 court judgments) it masks every mention of 93.4% of direct identifiers. On the six human-annotated exports of PrivacyBench v2.5, not inspected while the rules were written, it reaches 86.8% F1 (precision 88.1%, recall 85.6%) using export structure, and 81.9% F1 on text alone. It is weakest on organisation names (49.9% recall), links (61.9%), account numbers (68.3%) and street addresses (87.4%). We report the protocol, the published comparison table and the threats to validity. items.title: Deep Learning and Engineered Biomaterials‐Enhanced Imaging‐Guided Cancer Immunotherapy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The clinical success of immunotherapies is hindered by the absence of robust methodologies for the early and accurate assessment of antitumor immune responses. Integrating engineered biomaterials with artificial intelligence (AI)‐driven molecular imaging technology offers a powerful approach for predicting immune efficacy. However, its clinical translation is significantly hindered by several critical limitations, including the complex and costly synthesis of multifunctional imaging probes, insufficient deep‐tissue penetration, suboptimal in vivo signal‐to‐noise ratios, potential immunogenicity and off‐target toxicity, and the limited generalizability of deep learning models across heterogeneous patient populations. In view of these pressing scientific challenges, this review focuses on the application of chemical and biomolecular strategies‐enhanced engineered biomaterials in promoting the sensitivity and specificity of advanced imaging modalities for visualizing signaling molecules and immune cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME). Meanwhile, recent progress in deep learning‐driven image analysis has enabled strong predictive capabilities and automated the understanding of complex immune system dynamics. Together, these technologies provide a transformative platform for non‐invasive monitoring, personalized treatment, and response prediction, with the potential to advance precision immuno‐oncology and significantly impact both basic research and clinical translation.

items.title: DESIGNING RESILIENT ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS THROUGH AI-DRIVEN DEPENDENCY MAPPING AND IMPACT ANALYSIS
items.abstract: Enterprise systems are now often spread across a range of hidden technical and organizational dependencies; technical debt can accumulate, configurations can change, and failures can propagate. Redundancy or post-incident recovery alone is not enough for resilience design; such environments require continuously updated dependency knowledge and credible impact analysis before, during, and after change. This review considers peer-reviewed journal literature published between 2015 and 2024 that is relevant to the dependency mapping and impact analysis of resilient enterprise systems using AI. The studies included in the review are grouped around microservice architecture, process mining, digital twins, graph learning, anomaly detection, explainable artificial intelligence and resilience measurement, as well as AIOps. Based on the literature, it is shown that AI-based mapping can increase observability of runtime relations, aid in change-risk prioritization, and aid in failure localization with architectural models and operational telemetry. There are still gaps in causal validation, cross-layer dependency representation, data quality, explainability and evaluation against real enterprise incidents. There is scholarly value in the field, as resilient design increasingly relies on dynamic, evidence-based knowledge of how enterprise elements behave under stress, change and degradation.

items.title: Die Demokratisierung der künstlichen Intelligenz – Wie man eine KI sicher macht
items.abstract: Deutsch Dieses Konzeptpapier aus dem Jahr 2023 stellt einen Ansatz zur Demokratisierung künstlicher Intelligenz vor. Ziel ist die Entwicklung einer künstlichen demokratischen Intelligenz, deren Entscheidungsgrundlagen und Verhaltensregeln durch einen strukturierten demokratischen Dialog mit Menschen bestimmt und fortlaufend überprüft werden. Das Konzept beruht auf vier Demokratieaxiomen sowie den menschlichen Grundwerten Glück, Selbstbestimmtheit und Freiheit. Es unterscheidet zwischen Mikro-, Meso-, Makro- und Meta-Ebenen menschlicher Interaktion und entwickelt daraus eine sogenannte „Innere Direktive“ für künstliche Intelligenz. Im Mittelpunkt steht ein mehrstufiger demokratischer Dialogprozess, in dem eine KI als Moderatorin unterschiedliche Positionen zusammenführt, Kompromisse erarbeitet, Abstimmungen organisiert und Entscheidungen einer wiederkehrenden Evaluation unterzieht. Der Ansatz soll insbesondere verhindern, dass Mehrheitsentscheidungen grundlegende Interessen von Minderheiten verletzen. Anhand der Personalisierung von KI-Assistenten wird der vorgeschlagene Prozess exemplarisch dargestellt. Autor: Arnold Pohn-DudaOriginalfassung: 17. Juni 2023DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23452894 English This concept paper, originally written in 2023, presents an approach to the democratization of artificial intelligence. Its objective is to develop a form of democratic artificial intelligence whose decision-making principles and behavioral rules are established and continuously reviewed through a structured democratic dialogue with humans. The concept is based on four axioms of democracy and the fundamental human values of happiness, self-determination, and freedom. It distinguishes between micro-, meso-, macro-, and meta-levels of human interaction and derives an “Internal Directive” for artificial intelligence. At its core is a multi-stage democratic dialogue process in which AI acts as a moderator, brings together opposing perspectives, facilitates compromises, organizes voting, and subjects decisions to recurring evaluation. The approach aims, in particular, to prevent majority decisions from violating the fundamental interests of minorities. The proposed process is illustrated through an example involving the personalization of AI assistants. items.abstract: Digital pedagogy has become an essential component of higher education, offering new opportunities to develop students’ critical thinking, analytical reasoning, problem-solving, and independent learning skills. This article examines how digital learning environments and technology-enhanced teaching strategies can support the development of critical thinking among university students. Particular attention is given to blended learning, problem-based learning, collaborative digital platforms, and artificial intelligence. The discussion draws on existing research and identifies practical approaches for integrating digital tools into higher education. The article argues that technology alone does not guarantee improved learning outcomes; effective digital pedagogy requires purposeful instructional design, active student participation, and continuous feedback.

items.title: Electrodermal activity as a physiological marker of stress and experience-related differences in workers performing work at heights: A real-world functional data analysis study of certified and novice firefighters
items.abstract: Falls from heights remain a leading cause of fatal workplace accidents, with psychological stress contributing to human error. Electrodermal activity (EDA) and heart rate (HR) are promising stress markers whose real-world, physically demanding applicability remains underexplored. This study examined whether EDA and HR discriminate stress responses between certified and basically trained firefighters, and how these responses evolve across task phases. Seventeen male firefighters from the Moravian-Silesian Region, Czech Republic, completed an ascent, tower-top stay, and rappel from a 50-meter industrial cooling tower. EDA was recorded at the wrist and lumbar region using Sensetio wearable sensors, and HR via a Polar H10+ chest strap. After visual inspection, SCL was extracted from EDA; SCL and HR were both resampled to 600 samples (200 per phase) and min–max normalized. Functional data analysis using point-wise Mann–Whitney U tests, complemented by a cluster-based permutation test for multiple comparisons, compared SCL and HR between groups. SCL increased in both groups, but novices showed an earlier, steeper rise during the ascent and tower-top phases, forming two significant clusters after permutation correction ( t ≈ 59 –213, p c l u s t e r = 0.026 ; t ≈ 219 –421, p c l u s t e r = 0.017 ) with large effect sizes (median r = 0.71 ), whereas certified firefighters showed marked increases mainly during rappelling, where the difference narrowed and lost significance (median r = 0.46 ). No significant between-group HR differences emerged. Normalized SCL trajectories thus captured experience-related timing differences that HR did not, suggesting EDA warrants further investigation as a complement to safety training and monitoring, rather than as a validated readiness or error-risk-prediction tool at this stage.

items.title: Enhancing Liver Cirrhosis Diagnosis Using Machine Learning With Explainable AI and Cross-Validated Hyperparameter Tuning Techniques
items.abstract: Cirrhosis is a form of Chronic Liver Disease (CLD) resulting from sustained liver damage from several causes, including viral infection, autoimmune disorders, cholestatic and metabolic disease Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) or heavy alcohol use. Testing for the presence of Liver Cirrhosis (LC) is one of the most critical diagnostics and prognostic assessments for patients. Detecting liver illness in its early stages is challenging as initial symptoms are often mild and difficult to diagnose. Cirrhosis may not present symptoms until an advanced stage, posing a challenge for identification and diagnosis. The lack of explanations for a complex model’s decision-making process creates clinician distrust by concealing the reasoning behind its choices. This research sought to design and assess a novel and non-invasive proposed model by utilizing the XGBoost classifier with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for diagnosing liver cirrhosis. In this work XAI framework enhances transparency in complex models, offering valuable insights into decision-making, thereby guiding treatment strategies, and improving cirrhosis diagnosis. The experimental results have shown superiority for the proposed method compared with various machine learning models. The proposed method has achieved significantly 91.19% using XGBoost for cirrhosis dataset with K-fold validation(K=10) approach.

items.title: Ethics and Governance in the Age of Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Lifecycle Engineering Perspective
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Trustworthy Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is often treated as a model property addressed through better training data, alignment, evaluation or guardrails. We argue instead that trustworthiness is a lifecycle governance capability that must be engineered, evidenced, monitored and adapted across data acquisition, training and alignment, safe inference, public deployment and post‐deployment use. We develop a lifecycle engineering framework integrating four governance layers – technical, organizational, human‐centred and regulatory – and translate ethical principles and major governance instruments into stage‐specific controls, responsibilities, evidence artefacts, metrics and review triggers. The framework is constructed through a structured conceptual synthesis of peer‐reviewed literature, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 23894, ISO/IEC 42005, ALTAI, the EU AI Act and complementary security and agentic‐governance guidance. A source register, seven‐field extraction schema, explicit mapping rules, worked extraction example and weighting sensitivity analysis make the construction logic inspectable. A public‐facing retrieval‐augmented generation case and a contrastive agentic‐system stress test illustrate operationalization through measurable indicators, responsible actors, review triggers and capability boundaries without being presented as independent empirical validation. We further address hallucination, prompt injection, privacy leakage, overreliance, unsafe tool use, memory, planners and multi‐agent workflows. The perspective positions trustworthy GenAI as an evidence‐driven, adaptive socio‐technical capability rather than a one‐time model or compliance claim.

items.title: Evidence-State Drift: A Claim-Level Framework and Replay Benchmark for Web-Connected LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces Evidence-State Drift, a claim-level framework for monitoring changes in evidence used by web-connected large language model (LLM) agents over repeated retrieval events. The framework represents evidence using a normalized claim, evidence span, source identity, retrieval and publication timestamps, content fingerprint, and source-authority label. It aims to distinguish material changes in claim-associated evidence from non-material modifications, such as formatting changes, that do not alter the monitored claim. The study evaluates the proposed representation using a longitudinal replay benchmark containing 67 claims and 871 observation events, including 47 oracle-defined material changes. Within this benchmark, the claim-state detector achieved an F1 score of 0.989 against a predefined deterministic change oracle, with no false positives among 824 oracle-defined non-material events. These results indicate consistency with the benchmark’s predefined change rules. They do not establish independent semantic validation or improved factual accuracy in deployed LLM agents. Independent human evaluation and end-to-end agent testing remain areas for future work. This research contributes to the study of evidence monitoring, information freshness, data provenance, and reliability in web-connected AI systems.

items.title: Examining the Possible Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Educational Institutions: A Preliminary Investigation into Management Colleges in Jaipur
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has established itself as an engine for change in a variety of disciplines, reinventing operations, making decisions, and processes. AI has incredible potential in education that could enhance educational experiences, optimise administrative processes, and promote personalised education (Sadiku, M. N. et al, 2022). As educational institutions attempt to meet the needs of the digital age, investigating AI applications becomes critical (Pedro, F., et al., 2019). This early inquiry intends to look into the potential uses of AI in management colleges in Jaipur, India. The incorporation of AI into educational institutions has the potential to overcome a number of difficulties that exist in the traditional educational framework. As stated by Rane, N. et al. (2023), AI-powered technology can provide personalised learning experiences tailored to specific student needs, increasing student engagement and boosting learning results. Furthermore, AI-driven analytics can provide useful insights into studentperformance trends, allowing for early intervention measures to address academic issues (Jones et al., 2019). The landscape of AI use in educational institutions is rapidly changing. AI-powered chatbots are being used by institutions around the world to handle administrative activities like admissions, course registrations, and student inquiries (Alvarez, 2018). Furthermore, AI-powered learning management systems (LMS) are being used to provide adaptive learning experiences that dynamically modify content delivery based on student success and personal preferences (Wang et al., 2021)

items.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Management Information Systems: From Prediction to Managerial Decision-Making
items.abstract: The use of machine-learning models in management information systems enables organizations to generate predictions at increasing scale and speed. Predictive performance alone, however, is insufficient for managerial use. Decision makers also need to examine why an output was produced, interpret the explanation within the decision context, and monitor the consequences of resulting actions. This chapter treats explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) as an intermediate layer between machine-learning predictions and managerial decision-making. It integrates the literatures on decision support systems, human collaboration with artificial intelligence (AI), and human-centered XAI evaluation. To maintain a focused technical scope, the chapter examines two widely used methods for explaining the outputs of trained models: Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Drawing on the literature reviewed, the chapter develops a four-layer framework that connects prediction, explanation, managerial interpretation and evaluation, and decision, action, and feedback. Published studies from manufacturing, finance and credit, and energy management are then used to examine how these four layers appear in different application settings. The analysis indicates that explanations do not automatically produce trust, decision quality, or ethical acceptability. Their managerial value depends on the joint evaluation of technical properties, user and task characteristics, organizational context, and governance arrangements.

items.title: Explainable temporal deep learning for early prediction of concrete compressive strength using IoT sensor data
items.abstract: Concrete compressive strength is a fundamental indicator of structural performance, yet conventional destructive testing methods require 7–28 days, limiting timely decision-making in construction projects. This study presents an interpretable deep learning framework for early prediction of concrete compressive strength using real-time multivariate Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data. The proposed approach integrates internal curing conditions (temperature and humidity), ambient environmental variables, and mix design parameters to model early-age hydration dynamics as a temporal learning problem. A Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) network with an attention mechanism is developed to capture both forward and backward temporal dependencies in the curing process while identifying the most influential time intervals. To ensure interpretability, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and attention-based analysis are incorporated to quantify feature importance and reveal critical curing stages governing strength development. The model is trained and validated using field data collected from real construction sites, enabling evaluation under realistic environmental variability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high predictive accuracy (MAE = 1.52 MPa, R 2 = 0.94), outperforming benchmark models including GRU, Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), and conventional machine learning approaches. Unlike existing studies that primarily rely on laboratory-controlled datasets or focus on prediction without early-stage applicability, the proposed framework enables reliable estimation of 7-day and 28-day compressive strength within the first 24–48 h of curing. This combination of real-time IoT sensing, temporal deep learning, and explainable artificial intelligence provides a robust and practical decision-support tool for smart construction systems, enabling improved quality control, optimized scheduling, and reduced reliance on destructive testing.

items.title: Explaining cyberbullying and cyber violence in the age of AI using individual and contextual factors in Jordan
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies continue to transform online communication and social interactions, cyberbullying and cyber-violence have emerged as growing concerns that require a deeper understanding of the individual and contextual factors underlying these behaviors. This study aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the factors influencing cyberbullying and cyber-violence in Jordan. Specifically, it examines the effects of individual characteristics and contextual factors, including the legal and policy environment and aggressive social environment, on both cyberbullying and cyber-violence. A total of 472 participants from different demographic groups were included in the study sample. The data were analyzed using Smart PLS software. The results indicate that individual factors such as age, gender, and educational level have varying effects on cyberbullying and cyber-violence. Both age and gender have a significant negative and positive relationship, respectively, with both cyberbullying and cyber-violence. There is no significant relationship between these outcomes and educational level. Contextual factors, on the other hand, have differential effects. The aggressive social environment is positively associated with cyberbullying and cyber-violence, while the legal and policy environment is negatively associated with cyber-violence but not with cyberbullying. This study examines both contextual and individual factors, contributing to a better understanding of factors influencing cyberbullying and cyber-violence. It provides evidence on the impact of age, gender, social context, and legal and regulatory influences, and offers insights that can guide policy, education, and community engagement and inform best prevention practices.
